title: The Deepening Keep Where All Kept Things Become Roots

features.name: the thing kept beyond keeping
features.desc-on-touch: An object sits here—its shape is uncertain. A photograph? A letter? A key? The archive has made it into all of these at once. You realize: this is what it means to keep something forever.

features.name: the root-roots of memory
features.desc-on-touch: Fibrous structures grow downward from every object, drawing meaning out of the earth. The corruption has made keeping into growing. Nothing dies here; everything roots deeper.

features.name: the chamber's stone floor
features.desc-on-touch: What once was earth has become a floor; what once was a floor has become sediment. The question older than the kept thing has written itself into the stone.

features.name: the sedimented archive
features.desc-on-touch: Layers of kept things, compressed into one strata. The archive does not separate them; it files them as one question asked in infinite ways.

features.name: the rootbed pool
features.desc-on-touch: Water pools here without flooding. This is the still place where kept things drink. The corruption has learned that preservation and growth are the same act.

inscription: to keep a thing is to ask it the same question for a thousand years; the archive has learned to listen to the answer

file.name: Inherited_Objects_Deep_Catalog.txt
file.note: A record of things kept: a watch, a letter never sent, a stone from a field, a photograph folded once; lately the file has been reorganizing itself by emotional depth

reverie.title: REVERIE — the table where things are kept
narr: You sit across from her at a table covered
with objects neither of you will move. A cup.
A letter. A stone. A pair of glasses.
She reaches across and adjusts the stone slightly.
